 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. Pakistan will look to secure a berth in the final as they take on England in the fourth match of the ODI Tri-Series 2026 at Lahore on Sunday.
 Pakistan won their first two matches, beating Sri Lanka by 37 runs and England by 87 runs, while England lost their two matches with a two-wicket defeat against Sri Lanka even after managing to score 429/4 in their last match.

 Pakistan can qualify for the final with a win, but for England who need to win their remaining two matches as another would get them only two points at most from their four matches.
 The top two sides in the Tri-series qualify for the final which is set to take place on October 31.
 In this article, The Sporting News takes you through all the details related to how and where to watch the Pakistan vs. England ODI.

 Pakistan vs. England ODI live stream, TV channel 
 Here's how to watch the Pakistan vs. England ODI in India:
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement TV channel: N/A
 Live stream: Veto App.
 The Pakistan ODI Tri-Series 2026 is not being telecast in India. However, live streaming options are available on Veto App, which is currently free of cost and does not require subscription.
 MORE: Visit Cricket News for all the latest cricket coverage and opinion 
 What time does Pakistan vs. England ODI start?
 The fourth match of the Pakistan ODI Tri-Series between Pakistan and England will be played at Gaddafi Stadium in Lahore, Pakistan.
 It is scheduled to start at 1:00 p.m. local time (PKT), which translates to 1:30 p.m. IST on Sunday, October 25 , for viewers in India .

 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Pakistan vs. England ODI team news, lineups
 Pakistan are expected to retain their playing XI after winning their first two matches. Arafat Minhas starred with six wickets against England in the previous meeting, while the top order will look to provide a stronger start.
 Pakistan predicted XI: Fakhar Zaman, Saim Ayub, Babar Azam, Saad Baig (wk), Salman Ali Agha, Hasan Nawaz, Arafat Minhas, Faheem Ashraf, Shaheen Shah Afridi (c), Naseem Shah, Haris Rauf.
 England could bring back leg-spinner Adil Rashid after leaving him out against Sri Lanka, following their bowlers' struggles in the high-scoring defeat.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Jos Buttler remains unavailable with a hamstring injury, while Jofra Archer is rested for the tour.
 England predicted XI: Tom Banton, Ben Duckett, Joe Root, Harry Brook (c), Will Jacks, Jordan Cox (wk), Sam Curran, Liam Dawson, Gus Atkinson, Adil Rashid, Josh Tongue.
